subject: Math
prompt:
[Figure 1]

The height of each seedling in two groups, X and Y, was recorded. The histograms represent the distributions of height, in millimeters, for the seedlings in groups X and Y. The mean height of the seedlings in group X is equal to $20$, and the mean height of the seedlings in group Y is equal to $50$.

Which of the following statements about the standard deviations of height for the seedlings in these two groups is true?

choices.A: The standard deviation of height for the seedlings in group X is less than the standard deviation of height for the seedlings in group Y.
choices.B: The standard deviation of height for the seedlings in group X is equal to the standard deviation of height for the seedlings in group Y.
choices.C: The standard deviation of height for the seedlings in group X is greater than the standard deviation of height for the seedlings in group Y.
choices.D: There is not enough information to compare the standard deviations of height for the seedlings in these two groups.

explanation: Choice C is correct. Standard deviation measures the spread of a data set from its mean; a larger standard deviation indicates values are more dispersed from the mean, while a smaller standard deviation indicates values are more concentrated near the mean. The histogram for group X shows a bimodal distribution with $7$ seedlings in the $10$ to $14$ millimeter interval and $7$ seedlings in the $26$ to $30$ millimeter interval, while the middle intervals have much lower frequencies. Since the mean of group X is $20$ millimeters, many seedlings have heights approximately $8$ to $10$ millimeters away from the mean. In contrast, the histogram for group Y shows a unimodal distribution with $11$ seedlings concentrated in the $48$ to $52$ millimeter interval, which is very close to the mean of $50$ millimeters, and relatively few seedlings in the tail intervals. Since group X has more values dispersed far from its mean while group Y has most values clustered near its mean, group X has greater spread from its mean than group Y. Therefore, the standard deviation of height for the seedlings in group X is greater than the standard deviation of height for the seedlings in group Y.
